key_insight: The paper argues that long-horizon instability in latent surrogate solvers is not caused by using a latent space itself, but by how that latent space is trained and optimized. By learning latent representations that are stable under rollout, the model can preserve accuracy over much longer simulations.
problem_solved: It addresses error accumulation in neural surrogate solvers for time-dependent physical systems, where autoregressive predictions drift and become unreliable during long rollouts.
method: Train latent representations specifically for rollout stability, not just reconstruction or compression.
Use latent dynamics that remain consistent over many time steps, reducing compounding prediction errors.
Evaluate the learned representation in long-horizon surrogate simulation settings to verify stability and predictive fidelity.
impact: This matters for practitioners building physics-informed AI and surrogate simulators because it can make fast models usable for longer, more realistic simulations. It shifts the focus from simply compressing data to designing latent spaces that support stable prediction over time.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing full-resolution fields compressed into a latent space and rolled out over time.
A side-by-side plot comparing unstable latent rollout vs stable latent rollout with error growth curves.
An icon-based schematic of compression, dynamics, and reconstruction stages.
A timeline visualization showing short-horizon accuracy versus long-horizon drift.
paper_title: Beyond Compression: Training Latent Representations for Stable Long-Horizon Rollout in Neural Surrogate Solvers
paper_authors: Andreas E. Robertson, Ashley T. Lenau, John D. Shimanek, Benjamin A. Jasperson, Vivek Oommen
